items.evidence: "Speaker 2 opened the functional design meeting at 12:13 with a 40-minute agenda. The agenda includes reviewing minutes, discussing general objectives, three presentations, new project requirements, and deciding on remote control functions."

"75% of subjects found remotes ugly, while 80% would pay more for a 'fancier' looking device", "frustration with losing remotes", "users only utilize about 10% of available buttons, primarily focusing on volume and channel changes"; younger users wanting voice recognition appears later as "younger users (ages 15-35) interested in voice recognition".
"Speaker 5 discussed the technical aspects of designing a communication device that sends messages to a television. The presentation emphasized the need for prototypes to gather feedback..."
"A comparison was made between engineering-based designs with many features and basic designs with essential functions only."
"Speaker 4 explained the working design process... The proposed schematic includes four main components: an energy source, a chip to convert data, a user interface, and an infrared bulb."

New requirements section (teletext, TV only, corporate image) plus "Target Group and Core Functions" covering target group, voice recognition, locating a lost remote, and the charging cradle instead of batteries.
Action Items section says "(none)"; the questionnaire and summary are not mentioned anywhere.
No mention of the thirty minutes of individual work.
No mention of the project manager posting minutes and project documentation.
No mention of team members posting their documentation.
No mention of the components concept assignment.
No mention of the user interface concept assignment.
No mention of trend watching.
"Speaker 2 announced that the team will not include teletext functionality as it has been replaced by the internet."
"The project scope is strictly limited to television remotes to avoid unnecessary complexity."
"The design must incorporate the corporate image, specifically using yellow and black colors and the company slogan."
"The group decided on core design principles of simplicity, fashion, and usability."

Notes only say "The team discussed targeting a demographic of teenagers and families or those under age 65" and never state the conclusion that the team would define objectives (fashion, simplicity) instead of an age-based target group.
"Agreed functions include ... a way to locate the remote if lost." (Though the Summary separately lists a find-my-remote beep as an unresolved question, see errors.)
"Agreed functions include large buttons for essentials"
"Agreed functions include ... hidden secondary functions" and "keeping secondary settings less prominent"
"hidden secondary functions"

Notes say the charging cradle was only "considered" / "Potential Innovations: Consider a charging cradle" and list it under unresolved questions; transcript has the project manager say "that's a good idea, we'll keep it."
"The group discussed defining a target demographic, weighing the benefits of targeting younger users (ages 15-35)... versus a broader age range"
"Voice recognition was largely dismissed due to high production costs and potential complexity for the target user."
The discussion of how to make infra-red more functional (battery, chip quality, component quality) is absent; notes only carry the presentation point "a reliable infrared signal".
"The team also considered using a charging cradle instead of traditional batteries" and "Could we implement a rechargeable battery system..."

errors.claim: Speaker 5 discussed the technical interface, noting the need to balance conventional button placement with novel features like potential LCD screens or sliding hatches to hide complex functions.
errors.why_wrong: The LCD screen idea was raised by the marketing expert in her presentation, not by the user interface designer; the sliding hatch came up in the later group discussion (marketing expert's pull-out idea, user interface designer noting such remotes exist), not in his presentation.

errors.claim: Management decided against including teletext support or voice recognition due to complexity, cost, and changing consumer habits.
errors.why_wrong: Management ruled out teletext only; voice recognition was dropped by the team itself in discussion (user interface designer citing the 12.5 euro production limit, others agreeing).

errors.claim: Unresolved Questions: Would adding a "find my remote" beep function fit within budget?
errors.why_wrong: Nobody raised budget about this feature; the group agreed to include a way to find a lost remote ("Yeah, that'll probably be good", "so we want something to keep it from getting lost" - "Yep", "Yeah").

errors.claim: Unresolved Questions: Could we implement a rechargeable battery system that doubles as a storage solution?
errors.why_wrong: The project manager closed this with "that's a good idea, we'll keep it"; it was kept, not left open.
